title: A Prayagraj court’s summons to Independent MP Pappu Yadav for his skit at Parliament complex over the alleged theft of donations at Ram Temple raises the question of territorial jurisdiction
author: Krishnadas Rajagopal
content_html:
A Prayagraj court’s summons to Independent MP Rajesh Ranjan alias Pappu Yadav for his skit at the Parliament complex over the alleged theft of donations at the Ram Temple raises the question of territorial jurisdiction, which the judiciary is expected to strictly enforce to prevent “forum-shopping” by unscrupulous litigants as a means to harassment.

The court summons to the MP to reportedly appear before it on August 11 was based on a complaint filed before the court in Prayagraj. Section 223 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) begins with the words ‘A Magistrate having jurisdiction’, suggesting that the Magistrate should have territorial competence while taking cognisance of an offence on a complaint.

title: Amit Shah must answer for brutalities against students, says Rahul
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Sunday (August 9, 2026) mounted a sharp attack on Union Home Minister Amit Shah over the alleged use of batons and pellet guns against students protesting at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar on July 20. 

He said Mr. Shah would “sooner or later” have to answer for the “crime”.

In a post on X, Mr. Gandhi referred to a student he met at his ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ programme in Prayagraj on Saturday who, he claimed, told him that he had “no options left”.

The student had spent years preparing for examinations, sold family land and left his parents burdened with debt, Mr. Gandhi said. “This is not his failure, it is the failure of a system that refused to reward his hard work,” he said.

"अब मेरे पास कोई रास्ता नहीं बचा" - कल प्रयागराज में एक छात्र ने मुझसे यही कहा। सालों की तैयारी, घर की ज़मीन बेची, माँ-बाप का कर्ज़ और फिर भी हाथ में कुछ नहीं।

यह हार उसकी नहीं है। यह उस व्यवस्था की हार है जिसने उसकी मेहनत का दाम देने से इनकार कर दिया।

तेरह दिन हो गए - गृह…

— Rahul Gandhi (@RahulGandhi) August 9, 2026

The Opposition leader said several days had passed since the students called off their agitation over paper leaks, but Mr. Shah had not spoken about the police action against them.

“Batons and pellets were used against young people on the streets of the capital — and you did not utter a single word. Sooner or later, you will have to answer for this crime,” he said.

The issue has also disrupted the Parliament, with the Opposition insisting that Mr. Shah make a statement in both the Houses on the police action.

Speaking to reporters in Alappuzha, Congress general secretary (organisation) K.C. Venugopal also targeted Mr. Shah and defended Mr. Gandhi’s student outreach in Uttar Pradesh’s Prayagraj. He alleged that the BJP government attempted to disrupt the event.

“Yogi Adityanath and Prime Minister Narendra Modi tried their best to disrupt that event in Allahabad. They even spread human waste along the path leading to the venue,” he said.

Mr. Venugopal said the venue was initially denied after pressure was allegedly exerted on the college management, but permission was eventually granted.

“But what was the scene witnessed there yesterday, in Allahabad? Those were not typical Congress workers, Youth Congress, or NSUI members. That was India’s real Gen Z,” he said, claiming that similar participation had been witnessed at programmes in Kota and Dehradun.

He also cited Mr. Gandhi’s interventions on behalf of students affected by police action, including those injured by pellet guns and female students who were allegedly beaten by male police personnel.

Asked about senior Congress leader Shashi Tharoor’s remarks comparing the response to Mr. Gandhi’s ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ programme with the Jantar Mantar protests led by Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), Mr. Venugopal said he had seen only media reports about the remarks but urged his party colleagues not to make statements that could “please the BJP”.

“The BJP will be delighted if someone finds fault with Rahul Gandhi or says two negative things about him,” he said, while adding that he did not believe Mr. Tharoor had made the remarks deliberately.

Speaking at an event in Maharashtra on Friday, Mr. Tharoor had acknowledged that his party’s students’ outreach did not resonate the same way as the CJP protests. A day later, he clarified that he was stressing the need for political parties to open their doors and create pathways for the next generation to gain power to shape politics.

title: Tunnel road a ‘real estate project in disguise’, contend citizen groups
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
Citizens opposing the Congress government’s ambitious tunnel road project have termed it “a real estate project in disguise.” The citizens’ group Bengaluru Praja Vedike (BPV), which is at the forefront of the campaign against the project, has written to all the city’s MLAs and MPs, urging them to reject it.

In a letter addressed to them, the group has termed it a “vanity infrastructure that repeats flyover failures” and urged them to embrace “evidence-based planning”. They have alleged that ancillary revenue in the form of real estate is being given “free” to the concessionaire, which they estimate could be as high as ₹30,000 crore for the entire concession period.

Coming ahead of the Monsoon Session of the Karnataka legislature, starting on August 13, this is expected to give the Opposition further ammunition, keen to put Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar in a tight spot. 

Intermodal hubs 

The draft concession agreement shows that the concessionaire is required to build intermodal hubs at the vertical shaft points to create parking spaces. These will come up at five key junctions: Hebbal, Palace Grounds/Mehkri Circle, Race Course, Lalbagh and Silk Board. A total of 6.13 acres of land at these locations will be handed over by the government to the concessionaire.

Documents show that the intermodal hubs will be five-floor plazas, comprising a platform level, a services floor, a car parking floor, and two floors for retail space. Bengaluru Smart Infrastructure Ltd. (B-SMILE) estimates that these hubs could generate annual revenues of ₹250 crore to ₹300 crore for the concessionaire. The draft concession agreement states that this revenue, termed “ancillary revenue”, “will not be included in the calculations for review of the concession period”. The concession period is 30 years, extendable up to 40 years.

FSI 5

However, the ancillary revenue will be much higher, contend citizen groups. The same draft concession agreement also noted, “With respect to the retail spaces, a maximum FSI of 5 is permitted for development for the Intermodal Hubs above the surface (being Transit Oriented Development).” 

This means the intermodal hubs need not be limited to five-floor buildings, but could also be developed as high-rises, creating greater commercial real estate opportunities, they contend.

“This is nothing but a free gift to private real estate developers to build on valuable prime central Bengaluru locations up to FSI 5. Conservative estimates put the real estate revenues upwards of ₹30,000 Crore during the concession period,” the letter argued. 

“If the ancillary revenue is considered in calculating Total Concession Value (TCV) of the project, we can probably have the tunnel roads not tolled at all. The tunnel road project clearly has a big, but hidden real estate component, and may go down the road of NICE Road, embroiled in similar controversies over the years,” said Satya Arikutharam, an independent urban mobility expert. 

‘Incentive’

B.S. Parhlad, Technical Director, B-SMILE, said ancillary revenue was an incentive provided by the government to attract firms to build the tunnel roads and was not illegal. B-SMILE documents show that the arrangement is modelled on similar agreements with concessionaires by the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey and the New York State Thruway Authority. The State government has already raised a ₹19,000-crore loan for Viability Gap Funding (VGF), amounting to 40% of the project cost of the Hebbal-Silk Board North-South Tunnel Road. Incentives in the form of ancillary revenue will be over and above this.

title: A flood of woes in Assam
author: Rahul Karmakar
content_html:
Tamuli Gaon, a village in eastern Assam’s Jorhat district, is about 40 kilometres west of neighbouring Sivasagar district’s Bihubar, the epicentre of destruction by one of Assam’s worst localised floods since the 1950s. The gushing waters that submerged much of Sivasagar and adjoining Charaideo districts on July 19–20 lost momentum by the time they reached the periphery of Tamuli Gaon, but inundated the surrounding, low-lying paddy fields, to turn this village of 110 families into an island.

The village’s Biju Kumar Sarmah, a teacher nicknamed Gospuli for his obsession with plantation drives to “reclaim what’s lost”, explains why Tamuli Gaon was spared. “The water did not have enough force to cut through the embankments in our area, unlike those a few kilometres to the east, toward Sivasagar district,” he says. He is not sure whether the distance from Bihubar would provide Tamuli Gaon with insurance against a bigger disaster, with at least two more months of rain to go this year. “The floodwaters have less than half the distance to travel from Bihubar to Tamuli Gaon than from Mon to Bihubar,” he says.

title: Encroachments demolished along Girivalam path in Tiruvannamalai
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
Encroachments, mostly houses and petty shops, were demolished near Arunachaleshwarar temple along the Girivalam path in Tiruvannamalai town to ensure safety of pedestrians.

Officials of State Highways, which executed the work, said that along with the local police, demolition of encroachments was done along the 14-km Girivalam path.

Most of the encroachments on the path, especially towards Chengam Road, were built many years ago. The razed structures are mostly extensions of shops and commercial establishments. “Illegal construction, especially petty shops and push carts, have not only affected traffic movement, but it also reduced road space for pedestrians, who were forced to walk on the carriageway, risking their lives,” S. Anbarasu, Assistant Executive Engineer (AEE), State Highways (Tiruvannamalai), told The Hindu.

Officials said that the demolition drive was also meant to restore the original width of the path around the temple. The encroachments blocked free flow of excess rainwater on old narrow drains during monsoon, resulting in waterlogging.

“Each stretch around the temple should have a dedicated footpath with barricades for pedestrians. Roadside shops should be given separate space rather than encroaching carriageways,” said G. Pavitra, a resident.

Of the total distance of 14 km, identified encroachments were demolished to a distance of five km along the path. Encroachments had also reduced the total width of the carriageway by half. The stretch, which connects other key streets in town, has been used to pull the temple car during the Karthigai Deepam festival every year.

Highways officials said that as part of ensuring safety of devotees, overhead cables, including Tangedco power lines and internet cables, were replaced with underground cables. Tiled footpaths were also laid to provide more road space for pedestrians.
